newsitem.title: USA: Dayton shares rise on Mervyn's store cuts.
newsitem.headline: Dayton shares rise on Mervyn's store cuts.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp shares rose 1-1/4 to 38-1/8 at midday Friday after the company said its Mervyn's division will pull out of Florida and Georgia and sell 10 other poorly performing stores in other markets.
"Those were the markets that were having difficulty," Merrill Lynch analyst Daniel Barry said, referring to Florida and Georgia.
He added that Mervyn's, which has the bulk of its 300 stores in California, faced "long lines of distribution" in Florida and Georgia.
Mervyn's plans to exit Florida and Georgia are part of broader efforts by Dayton to turn that division around, Barry said.
As previously reported, Mervyn's same store sales for the year-to-date period ended January 4 were off 4.3 percent.
"I'm sure Florida and Georgia are the areas where they're missing plan the most," Barry said.
